I’d tell you it gets better, but as someone who in the past few weeks has felt that way every second of almost every day, I can’t tell you that. It doesn’t always get better, but it can get easier. One thing that’s helped is to find something, anything to look forward to, even if it’s just getting up at all, if it’s just managing to wake up without immediately feeling like I’m dying. The small victories can lead to so much bigger victories, you just have to find something to keep you going. Just last one more second, just last one more minute, one more hour, one more day, and just keep lasting one more moment, until it gets easier to last so many more. I can’t tell you to ‘just get over it’ or ‘you’ll be okay if you just try harder’ because that’s not how it works. The best you can do is to keep yourself alive. Even if you can’t eat, can’t sleep, just managing to put something in your stomach, just managing to rest for even an hour or so, that is so much better than just sitting there in your emotions, because while it’s important to give yourself time to process your emotions, it’s also important to give yourself time to recover, to rest, to relax, even if it’s not the healthiest thing out there, sometimes you just need to find something mindless, something that makes it so you can breathe, even for a second. You can do this. As someone very important to me said whenever Im in my darkest moments, ‘you don’t have to believe in yourself, but can you trust me that I do?’ Do you trust me enough to trust that I believe in you? That I believe that you can do this, even if the process is slow? Even if you have the worst moments you think you’ve ever experienced, do you trust that I believe in you? I hope you do, because I believe in you. Truly.
